ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure is a schematic diagram of a small AC generator. The coil $ABCD$ has $n=200$ turns and an area of $S=0.01\mathrm{m}^{2}$. The resistance is negligible, and it rotates uniformly around the axis $oo$ perpendicular to the magnetic field with an angular velocity of $\omega=100\mathrm{rad/s}$. The magnetic induction intensity of the uniform magnetic field is $B=\sqrt{2}\mathrm{T}$. The coil is connected to an ideal transformer via slip rings, and the secondary coil is connected to a resistor $R$. All meters are ideal, and the ammeter reads $I=2\mathrm{A}$. Timing starts when the coil is at the neutral plane position.

1. What is the instantaneous value expression of the induced electromotive force in the wire frame?
2. What is the reading on the voltmeter?
3. When the turns ratio of the primary to secondary coil is 2:1, what is the resistance value of resistor $R$?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a rectangular coil ABCD located between the N and S magnetic poles; the coil is led out through two slip rings and brushes; the coil rotates around the axis oo marked in the figure (the direction of the dashed axis in the figure). In the circuit on the right, the coil output is connected to the primary coil of an ideal transformer, voltmeter V is connected in parallel across the two ends of the primary coil, and ammeter A is connected in series in the primary coil circuit; the secondary coil is connected to resistor R. Reasoning: The problem gives n=200, S=0.01 m^2, B=√2 T, ω=100 rad/s. The coil starts timing from the neutral plane, so the induced electromotive force starts from 0 and changes according to a sine law: e=E_m sin(ωt). The maximum electromotive force E_m=nBSω=200×√2×0.01×100=200√2 V, so e=200√2 sin(100t) V. The coil resistance can be ignored, and the slip rings to the primary coil of the transformer are an ideal connection, so the effective value of the voltage across the two ends of the primary coil is equal to the effective value of the generator electromotive force: U_1=E_m/√2=(200√2)/√2=200 V, so the voltmeter reading is 200 V. When the turns ratio of the primary and secondary coils is N_1:N_2=2:1, the ideal transformer satisfies U_1/U_2=N_1/N_2=2, so U_2=100 V. The ammeter reads the primary coil current I_1=2 A, and the current ratio of the ideal transformer is I_2/I_1=N_1/N_2=2, so I_2=4 A. The secondary coil is connected only to resistor R, so R=U_2/I_2=100/4=25 Ω.
